newsitem.title: USA: US West Coast Calif. crudes see action Wednesday.
newsitem.headline: US West Coast Calif. crudes see action Wednesday.

text.p: U.S. West Coast crude buying picked up Wednesday, with several shipments of California grades sold as the deadline for pipeline scheduling approached, traders said.
In futures markets, the July spot contract for West Texas Intermediate/Cushing (WTI) crude rose 27 cents a barrel below the previous session to $21.86 a barrel.
Traders said a large independent refiner based in California and Texas bought 5,000 barrels-per-day (bpd) of High Viscosity High Sulphur (HVHS) crude Wednesday for June delivery.
The grade is a combination of heavy offshore California grades and a small amount of lighter Line 63, which helps push it down ARCO's north-south pipeline into Los Angeles.
The refiner paid the price of offshore Point Arguello plus $4.25 a barrel to have the HVHS delivered to Los Angeles.
"They used to run Line 63, now they're not," one trader said, referring to the refiner, which runs a plant in Wilmington, Calif.
Heavier deliveries of Oriente have displaced the refiner's appetite for Line 63 in recent weeks, and its ability to process large amounts of high sulphur crude enable it to run HVHS, traders said.
"It's just balancing the refinery with foreign crude coming in," one trader said.
Meanwhile, Tosco bought Line 63 from the same refiner at postings plus 70 cents. Both sides confirmed the deal, which saw the Tosco take a 5,000 bpd delivery.
Texaco sold heavy crude at 10 to 15 cents under postings on Wednesday, one of its traders said, but a buyer did not immediately confirm the price or volume.
Benchmark West Coast grade, Alaska North Slope (ANS), tracked the rise in futures, hitting $20/20.20 a barrel, or a 40-cents rise from Tuesday.
ANS discounts have remained flat at $1.50 a barrel under WTI, with BP, a leading seller, keeping its offer at minus $1.30 Tuesday.
